Danis and Weber Classification of Malleolar Fractures of The Ankle

  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Definition

  • It is three grades system to classify malleolar fractures of the ankle joint
  • it is based on the location of the fibular fracture (lateral malleolar fracture) in relation to the level of the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis and as a result we have grade A that is below the level of syndesmosis and grade B at the level of syndesmosis and grade C above level of syndesmosis.
  • Reminder: distal tibiofibular syndesmosis is formed by the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament, posterior inferior tibiofibular ligament and the interosseous tibiofibular ligament
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Classification

  • Grade A: below level of syndesmosis
  • A1: isolated
  • A2: with medial malleolus fracture
  • A3: with fracture of the posteromedial part of the tibia
  • Grade B: at level of syndesmosis
  • B1: isolated
  • B2: with medial malleolus fracture or deltoid ligament injury
  • B3: with B2 and fracture of the posteromedial part of the tibia
  • Grade C: above level of syndesmosis
  • C1: simple diaphyseal fracture of the fibula
  • C2: complex diaphyseal fracture of the fibula
  • C3: proximal fracture of the fibula
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade A

  • Fracture location: below level of syndesmosis
  • Mechanism of injury: supination- adduction
  • Transverse fracture
  • Tibiofibular syndesmosis: intact
  • Medial malleolus: occasionally fractured
  • Deltoid ligament: intact
  • Fracture stability: stable if medial malleolus intact
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade B

  • Fracture location: At the level of syndesmosis
  • Mechanism of injury: supination- external rotation and pronation abduction
  • Spiral or oblique fracture
  • Tibiofibular syndesmosis: intact or partially torn
  • Medial malleolus: could be fractured
  • Deltoid ligament: could be torn
  • Fracture stability: Variable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade C

  • Fracture location: Above level of the syndesmosis
  • Mechanism of injury: pronation- external rotation
  • Tibiofibular syndesmosis: torn
  • Associated with medial malleolus fracture or deltoid ligament rupture
  • Fracture stability: unstable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden
